tagline: The score is a fact. The story gets checked.
MONETIZATION_RULE: STANDING RULE (strategy desk, 2026-07-21): NO monetization of any kind (ads, AdSense, affiliate links) on any page fed by MLB StatsAPI, NHL api-web, or ESPN endpoints (scoreboards, content API) until a formal terms review of those feeds is completed. Publishing unmonetized content from them continues as-is (acceptable use). Monetizing pages built on these feeds without that review is the quiet terms violation that gets API access cut. Any session wiring ads or affiliates MUST check this rule first. The per-feed terms flags live in sources.league_apis.note.

TOP_N_NOTE: TOP_N RULING 2026-07-31: cut from 12 to 8 per slot. The desks were publishing ~184 articles a week between them while all article pages combined drew ~16 weekly views, so slots 9 to 12 were reaching nobody. Cutting the tail reduces per-run spend (fewer researcher, writer, and verifier calls), raises the average significance of what reaches the front page, and lowers exposure to search-engine scaled-content policies, which target high-volume automated publishing. Revisit when distribution catches up to the inventory; this is a quality-over-volume decision, not a cost-only one.

budget.note: Fail-closed cap. The token and USD caps must express the SAME limit and they did not: 220k tokens fires at roughly $0.32-0.41 on Haiku while the USD cap allows $1.50, so the token cap was binding at about a quarter of the approved spend and a normal run already sat at 50-100% of it. A News run on 2026-07-31 drafted 8 of 8 stories and then died in the approver at 227,860 tokens, spending everything and publishing nothing. 400k keeps a full run near $0.60, still well under the USD cap, which is now the limit that actually binds. Cutting top_n from 12 to 8 was tried first and did not fix it.

researcher.note: Role 1 of the three-role editorial pipeline: builds the structured research brief (data points + confidence labels + the other side of the story) from the fetched source pages. Fact fidelity is the whole job. COST LOCKDOWN (owner directive 2026-07-21): Haiku, crypto-desk parity.
researcher.note_capacity: Output ceilings sized for a full 12-story day (2026-07-22: the researcher hit the 8000 cap on all three ladder rungs once the intake fattened; Haiku 4.5 allows 64k output, and a ceiling only bills when used).

writer.note: Full-length stories (350-650 words) in batches of 3 per call; the cap covers 3 complete drafts with headroom so JSON never truncates. COST LOCKDOWN (owner directive 2026-07-21): Haiku, crypto-desk parity.

approver.note: Role 3: post-draft last line of defense (accuracy/liability -> balance -> quality, categorized rejections). A different call from the writer so the builder never approves their own work.

models.note: COST LOCKDOWN (owner directive 2026-07-21, supersedes the quality-launch A/B): crypto is the priority bet and this desk must never run a higher cost than the crypto desk. claude-haiku-4-5 on every desk stage, exactly like crypto; the deterministic fail-closed gates (source liveness, dedup, depth gate, belts, corroboration rules) are the quality floor, not the model. wraprescue keeps claude-sonnet-5 for the rare edition-failure path only, same as crypto. REVERSAL TRIGGER: real audience traction on this desk -> revisit the writer model.

publicist.note: Publicist DISABLED per strategy 2026-07-21: LinkedIn is currently the government-sales channel. Code kept in the repo, schedule removed from publicist.yml. Re-enable only on explicit direction.

wrap.note: The Daily Edition (Morning Brief / Closing Wrap, wrap.py): synthesis over the desk's own published stories. COST LOCKDOWN (owner directive 2026-07-21): Haiku, crypto-desk parity.

wrapcheck.note: Independent trace check on the edition: every specific fact must come from the provided inputs; no betting advice or predictions; calm register. Separate call from the writer.

aging.note: Monthly post-publication review (aging.py, report-only): has any published story's premise been invalidated? Conservative flagging; a human decides on corrections.

wraprescue.note: The Daily Edition's second-chance generator: when the Haiku edition fails its trace check, the corrective rewrite runs here. CEILING RAISED 8000->16000 (owner ruling 2026-08-04): this stage returned empty responses that cost two editions; the diagnostics showed thinking consuming the whole output budget (stop_reason=max_tokens, blocks=['thinking'], out_tokens at the ceiling), leaving no text block.

sources.note: source_tier drives editorial weight. primary = official league/institutional sources (trust most: box scores, transactions, discipline rulings straight from the league). major = established outlets with editorial standards. mixed = aggregated or rumor-adjacent feeds (never publish alone; two-source rule applies). All feeds below are free and keyless, verified live 2026-07-19. The reliability layer is the pipeline (tiering, two-source corroboration, adversarial verifier, primary-source linking), not any single API.

rss.name: ESPN College Football
rss.note: RESTORED 2026-09-04. Retired 2026-09-03 as dead; it was not dead. The RSS host does answer datacenter IPs with an HTTP 202 bot challenge, which is real and unsolved, but the JSON fallback wired 2026-09-02 was returning 403 for one reason: the desk's branded User-Agent. ESPN's API tier allows generic HTTP client agents and rejects branded ones. common.ua_for now sends a generic client string to ESPN API hosts only. Proven from CI, not a laptop: the first scheduled run after the same fix landed in scores_pulse pulled 9 leagues and 29 games from site.api.espn.com on a GitHub runner. The RSS primary is still expected to fail from CI; espn_api_fallback is the working path.

sources.keywords_note: Optional per-feed 'keywords' gate: high-volume aggregated feeds keep only items matching a keyword in headline+snippet, so they cannot flood the editor. Items matching a 'narratives' watchlist entry always pass the gate.

league_apis.note: Official and quasi-official structured data endpoints, all keyless and verified live 2026-07-19. These are the desk's PRIMARY factual sources: the researcher and verifier treat league-published schedules, scores, and transactions as ground truth that outranks any outlet's retelling. balldontlie was dropped (now key-gated, 401). Upgrade path if the desk ever needs deeper stats: API-Sports (~$10/mo) or SportsDataIO, deliberately excluded from v1 under the free-only constraint. TERMS FLAGS: MLB StatsAPI is public but historically non-commercial terms; ESPN scoreboard/content endpoints are unofficial with no stated terms (revocable); NHL api-web is undocumented. See MONETIZATION_RULE at the top of this file: no ads or affiliate monetization on pages fed by these until a formal terms review.

sources.espn_note: ESPN RESTORED 2026-09-04 after the User-Agent was identified as the cause of the 403s that got these feeds retired on 2026-09-03. Two separate failures had been read as one: the RSS hosts answer datacenter IPs with HTTP 202 bot challenges (IP-based, still unsolved, no User-Agent fixes it), while the site.api/now.core JSON tier answers 403 to any branded agent (UA-based, fixed by common.ua_for). Because only the second was ever the blocker on the fallback path, espn_api_fallback now serves these lanes from CI. If ESPN 403s again, test the agent before retiring anything.

narratives.note: The desk's ongoing-storyline watchlist, maintained by the editor-in-chief. A cluster whose headline/snippet matches any keyword gets tagged with the narrative's name in items.json, the editor treats a genuine development in a tagged narrative as presumptively rank-worthy, and watchlist matches always pass a feed's keyword gate. Seeded for July 2026; add narratives as they emerge, retire them when they resolve.

dedupe.note: Near-identical stories across outlets (same event, many rewrites) collapse into one cluster by normalized-headline token overlap or shared URL. The cluster keeps the highest-tier source as primary and lists the rest as corroboration. CROSS-OUTLET SIGNAL (2026-07-31, news parity): headline-token Jaccard almost never fires across outlets wording the same event differently. A second conservative signal merges on shared distinctive entities (capitalized words and numbers) within a time window and above a token floor. Measured on news intake: corroboration 4% -> 8% with zero false merges; looser settings were REJECTED because they merged opinion columns with news as if they corroborated each other. BODY-TEXT MATCHING (2026-08-01): headlines are reworded freely across outlets, so headline signals alone found only 4% corroboration while a 20-of-20 hand sample showed every single-source story HAD other outlets on it. Entities are now also read from the feed's sentence-cased snippet (90% of items carry one), where a capitalised word is a real proper noun rather than Title Case. When the prose shares body_strong_entities distinctive specifics INCLUDING a number, that stands alone without the headline-overlap floor, which was gating out exactly the pairs body matching exists to catch.

publish.not_financial_advice: GoCheckMySports reports events. It never advises bets. Nothing here is betting or gambling advice.

top_n_note: Raised 8 -> 12 (owner directive 2026-08-20, 'we have to get the news out'). The editor ranks top_n stories per run and roughly half die at the approver, so 8 capped a run at about 4 published and pushed real news below the line: the day the desk missed an overnight missile barrage and a ballistic-missile launch it also ranked only 8 candidates. Budget headroom is real, a typical run costs $0.15-0.30 against a $1.50 fail-closed cap, and the cap still governs.

edition.note: EDITION FLOOR (family audit 2026-09-02): when the synthesis fails its gates after the deterministic sentence cuts and the Sonnet rescue, wrap.py publishes a plain digest built only from the desk's own published, verified stories (edition_repair.digest_edition) so the slot is served, the recovery net stops re-firing the whole pipeline, and the reader gets the day's verified news. Set false to restore fail-closed-to-silence.
